proposed_comments.title: Make launcher startup and teardown race-free
proposed_comments.body:
### Make launcher startup and teardown race-free

**Severity:** `high`

The native launcher sends its initial status immediately after starting the UI, before the WinUI pipe callback is guaranteed to be registered, so the only initial payload can be lost and the progress window can remain empty. The window-arranger callback also starts `Launch()` on a detached thread that captures `this`, while helper callbacks can remain active during destruction, and `LaunchingStatus::Get()` returns a reference after releasing its lock. Please add an explicit UI-ready handshake that resends a status snapshot, return status data by value, own and join the launch worker, and unregister/stop IPC callbacks before destroying the launcher-owned helpers.

proposed_comments.title: Complete cancellation before closing the UI
proposed_comments.body:
### Complete cancellation before closing the UI

**Severity:** `high`

The submitted `CloseButton_Click` closes the window without sending `cancel`, despite the validation claim, and the native cancellation handler only marks apps that are still `Waiting`. A launch iteration can select an app concurrently and later overwrite `Canceled` with `Launched` or `Failed`; closing the UI immediately also gives the user no confirmation that native cancellation completed. Separate Cancel from Dismiss, send `cancel`, atomically order cancellation with app claims and terminal state updates, acknowledge only after native state is updated, close on `cancel_ack`, and cover the full send/ack/close handshake with a test.

proposed_comments.title: Ship reliable installed launcher icons
proposed_comments.body:
### Ship reliable installed launcher icons

**Severity:** `medium`

`Package.Logo.LocalPath` does not reliably identify a concrete installed asset for packaged apps because manifests can use resource and qualified scale/target-size variants, and the WinUI `Assets\Workspaces` directory is not harvested by the installer changes in this PR. Installed builds can therefore miss both package icons and the default/window fallback icons. Resolve qualified package asset candidates, keep executable/PWA fallbacks, install the Workspaces asset directory under `WinUI3Apps`, and add coverage for packaged asset selection and missing-asset fallback.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve DPI, monitor-origin, and announcement context
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve DPI, monitor-origin, and announcement context

**Severity:** `medium`

The window is resized to a fixed 360 physical pixels and centered without adding `WorkArea.X/Y`, so it shrinks at higher scaling and is misplaced on monitors whose work area does not start at the virtual origin. The live status announcement also contains only the state, so Narrator cannot identify which app changed when several entries update. Size after activation using the active XAML rasterization scale, center within the full work-area rectangle, keep the Windows 10 custom-title-bar border workaround, and format each localized live announcement with both the application name and state.

test_instructions: Launch <PowerToysCheckout>\x64\Debug\PowerToys.exe and start a workspace containing several Win32, packaged, and PWA applications.
Verify the status window receives its initial list reliably, updates every app, and closes cleanly after completion.
Cancel while several apps remain pending; verify no additional pending apps launch, the native side acknowledges cancellation, and the UI closes only after the acknowledgment.
Verify packaged, PWA, executable, and missing-app icons resolve, including the installed DefaultIcon.ico fallback.
At 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling on monitors with non-zero virtual origins, verify the window remains approximately 360 logical pixels and is centered within the target work area.
With Narrator, verify each live announcement includes the application name and localized launch state; on Windows 10 verify the custom title bar retains the one-pixel top border.
